_comment: Superbad (2007) shot catalogue. Source cut runs ~113:30 of story + ~5min end credits (transcript duration 7120s; 40 overview montage pages at 36 frames/page, 5s per frame). depth_target: video_essay - the film is wall-to-wall dialogue comedy with a genuinely dense beat map, so coverage is per-visual-moment rather than per-camera-cut. PRE-CATALOGUE (A7): Wikipedia Plot + Cast read before tagging; Cast section cross-checked against the film's own end-credit crawl (pages 39-40) which is more precise than names.json for minor roles - it confirms 'Francis the Driver' = Joe Lo Truglio (the motorist who hits Seth) and 'Mark' = Kevin Corrigan (the party host in the yellow Brazil jersey who ejects Francis and later brawls with Seth). Frames win over Wikipedia where they disagree. SPOILER DISCIPLINE (A8): see _reveal_map below - this comedy has exactly two withheld-information beats and both live in the last 15 minutes. CHARS NOTE: names.json lists 'Fogell' and 'McLovin' as separate entries for the same actor and the same visible person; this catalogue uses 'Fogell' ONLY in chars so the binding audit never has to disambiguate one body into two names. Script writers should name him Fogell in claim.subject even when the narration says McLovin. CENSOR: R-rated raunch comedy - explicit content is frequent but mild and comic; blur_light for the porn magazine, the porn-site trailer, the penis drawings, the period-blood stain and the underwear-level bedroom beats, blur for the one actual sex scene (Fogell/Nicola). No gore anywhere in the film: the car hits, the punches and the cruiser crash are all played without injury detail, so they stay censor none.
_censor_note: S7 revision 2026-08-19: these levels were raised blur_light -> blur after blur_light was measured insufficient (line 8's magazine cover stayed legible through boxblur=15). DATA FIX ONLY - final.mp4 in this project predates it and still carries the old blur_light render. Re-render before republishing. Levels were judged from catalogue descriptions plus one verified frame (line 108 at 'blur' is adequately obscured); a human eye pass is still advised, especially clip:01:34:15.0 and clip:01:37:38.0 which may warrant blur_heavy.
_depth_note: MEASURED: 181 shots across 59 beats (~3.1/beat), against the video_essay band of 110-130. The overage is real, not padding: from 00:48:00 to 01:41:00 the film runs three storylines in parallel (Seth at Mark's party, Evan on the phone and then trapped on a couch, Fogell in the patrol car) and intercuts them continuously, so a single beat of screen time routinely contains two or three separate visual moments that cannot share a window. Every shot here is frame-verified against frames/overview and no window is duplicated. Do NOT trim this to hit the band - if a shorter recap is wanted, drop beats at the skeleton stage rather than starve the catalogue. 13 beats sit at one shot (B13, B19, B27, B41, B43, B44, B45, B47, B49, B50, B52, B54, B55); each was checked and is a genuine single moment (a pure establishing beat, a single held reaction, or a one-line hinge), not an oversight.

_zone_map.SETUP: 00:00:00 - 01:37:35. Everything a first-time viewer may be told plainly: the two seniors and their deadline, Jules' party and the liquor errand, Becca and Evan, Fogell's fake ID and the McLovin name, the failed buy, the robbery, the two officers collecting Fogell, the motorist, Mark's party, the brawl, the friendship fight, the cruiser hitting Seth, the escape, Jules' party and its three parallel disasters, the bust. The McLovin ID gag at 00:27:25 is a comic surprise, NOT a protected reveal - it is the film's advertised hook and the whole middle depends on the audience already being in on it.
_zone_map.REVEAL: 01:37:35 - 01:47:15. Two withheld-information beats, both late, both retro-active: R1 the officers admit they knew 'McLovin' was underage from the first minute and played along on purpose; R2 Seth confesses he found Evan's housing forms three weeks earlier and had known all night that Evan and Fogell were rooming together. Narration must not hint that the cops are in on it before 01:38:35, and must not hint that Seth already knows about the housing forms before 01:45:05 - both are the payoff for behaviour the audience has been reading as pure idiocy and pure selfishness respectively.

_reveal_map.label: The officers knew Fogell was underage the whole time
_reveal_map.note: Transcript-locked: 'You're not 25, man. We're not idiots, McLovin.' / 'Did you know the whole time?' / 'We're your age... we hated cops... we just wanted to show you cops can have a fun time too.' Before this, every cop scene must be narrated as two incompetents, because that is what the audience is watching.

_reveal_map.label: Seth already knew Evan and Fogell were rooming together
_reveal_map.note: Transcript-locked: 'I was in your room like three weeks ago... I saw your housing forms. So I knew you and Fogell were going to live together.' Recontextualises Seth's aggression across the whole night. Fogell's slip at the party (01:25:05) is the audience's first hint but NOT the reveal - Seth's reaction there must be narrated as fresh hurt.
